section.title: Introduction and Overview
section.p: ORAS is a command-line client for OCI registries. It exchanges RISC OS files as OCI fileset artifacts, allowing a group of files to be published to and retrieved from a registry without losing recognised RISC OS metadata.

The URLFetcher modules are required to use ORAS. They provide the HTTP and HTTPS transport used to communicate with an OCI registry. ORAS supports anonymous access to public registries and standard Basic and Bearer challenge authentication. Credentials are stored in Docker-compatible form in the file named by <ORASAuthentication$Write>. That file is not encrypted and should be protected with normal file access controls.

An OCI reference has the form registry.example.net/repository:tag. The registry host is mandatory. A tag is optional and defaults to latest; a digest selector may be used in place of a tag, for example registry.example.net/repository@sha256:....

section.title: Technical Details
section.p: ORAS filesets use an OCI image manifest with artifact type application/vnd.riscos.fileset.v1 and the manifest annotation org.riscos.artifact.format = fileset-v1. Each layer represents exactly one file; its blob is the unmodified file contents with media type application/riscos. Its org.opencontainers.image.title annotation is a portable relative output path. The accompanying org.riscos.filename annotation preserves the native RISC OS leaf name, including a suffix such as /xml.

When requested with --source, published manifests include the OCI source annotation org.opencontainers.image.source. The shorthand github:owner/repository expands to the corresponding GitHub repository URI. No source annotation is added by default.

When pushing, ORAS records any available file type, load address, execution address and attributes in the layer annotations org.riscos.filetype, org.riscos.loadaddr, org.riscos.execaddr and org.riscos.attr. When pulling, it creates parent directories, writes every blob, and then applies the recognised metadata. Absolute paths, empty path components, . and .. components are rejected to prevent writing outside the requested output directory.

Push arguments must be files, not directories. The stored output name is the RISC OS leaf name of each supplied path, so each push must have distinct leaf names. For example, prminxml.oras/xml is stored with native name oras/xml and portable title oras.xml. An OCI index can be pulled when it contains exactly one manifest; an index with multiple candidates cannot currently be selected from the command line.

command-definition.name: oras
command-definition.description: Uses OCI registry artifacts from RISC OS
command-definition.parameter: One of the operations described below.

use.p: Invoking *oras without a valid operation displays the available command syntax. The commands report an error when the registry does not accept the request or returns an unsuccessful HTTP status.

command-definition.name: oras pull
command-definition.description: Retrieves a RISC OS fileset artifact
command-definition.parameter: The OCI artifact reference to retrieve.
The destination directory. It defaults to the current directory.

use.p: Retrieves the manifest and each of its file layers. Files are recreated below the destination directory, with parent directories and recognised RISC OS metadata restored. Unsafe stored paths and duplicate output paths are refused.

command-definition.name: oras push
command-definition.description: Publishes files as a RISC OS fileset artifact
command-definition.parameter: The OCI artifact reference to publish.
A source file to include in the fileset.
An OCI source URI, or github:owner/repository.

use.p: Uploads each source file as a separate application/riscos OCI blob, records the file metadata where available, and publishes the fileset manifest. Directories are not accepted; provide every file explicitly. The optional source URI is recorded as org.opencontainers.image.source; it is not inferred from the target registry or repository.

command-definition.name: oras manifest fetch
command-definition.parameter: The OCI manifest reference to retrieve.
Optional destination file for the JSON.

use.p: Writes the manifest JSON to the optional file, or to standard output.

command-definition.name: oras blob fetch
command-definition.parameter: An OCI reference identifying the registry and repository.
The blob digest, such as sha256:....
Optional destination file for the blob.

use.p: Writes the blob bytes to the optional file, or to standard output.

command-definition.name: oras tags
command-definition.description: Lists tags in an OCI repository
command-definition.parameter: An OCI registry host and repository path.

use.p: Lists the repository tags, normally with one tag on each output line.

command-definition.name: oras login
command-definition.parameter: The exact registry host, optionally including its port.

use.p: Prompts for a non-echoed secret and stores a Docker-compatible auths entry. The credential file is not encrypted.

command-definition.name: oras logout
command-definition.parameter: The exact registry host, optionally including its port.

use.p: Removes only the matching credential entry from the configured credential file.
Runs non-network checks for reference parsing, fileset metadata, and safe file extraction. A successful run prints All self-tests passed.

subsection.title: Publishing and retrieving a fileset
subsection.p: This example publishes two files, then recreates them under a destination directory. The destination receives the content and recognised metadata stored in the artifact.

p.extended-example: *oras push registry.example.net/charles/demo:1.0 Apps.Demo,ff8 Docs.ReadMe,fff *oras pull registry.example.net/charles/demo:1.0 Work.Demo

subsection.title: Inspecting a published artifact
subsection.p: Fetch the manifest before retrieving a specific blob. The manifest supplies the digest and metadata for each file layer.

p.extended-example: *oras manifest fetch registry.example.net/charles/demo:1.0 DemoManifest,fff *oras blob fetch registry.example.net/charles/demo:1.0 sha256:0123456789abcdef... Blob,fff *oras tags registry.example.net/charles/demo
